newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on fresh buying.

text.p: Most Shanghai soybean futures contracts ended slightly up on Friday on speculative buying at low levels, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,409 yuan per tonne ($411), losing eight yuan. It opened at 3,390 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,418 and a low of 3,388 yuan.
May rose 13 yuan to 3,365, July four to 3,404, November three to 3,428 and the January 1998 contract three to 3,420.
Combined volume rose to 20,000 tonnes from 17,500 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and speculative buying at lower levels pushed most contracts up.
"Speculators for short-term profit built positions at low prices and the volume grew, which indicates soybeans will firm in the near future," said one trader.
Traders said technical charts also showed a rising trend but the lack of market-moving news will limit upward potential.
